newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: New Manila bourse head urges unity, end to feuds.
newsitem.headline: New Manila bourse head urges unity, end to feuds.

text.p: The Philippine Stock Exchange's new president on Sunday called for an end to squabbles and said that unity among capital market players was needed to help the PSE become a world class bourse.
Vitaliano Nanagas, who starts his three-year term on Monday, said the potential of the PSE "to grow and be at par with the region's best is realisable sooner than we think."
But unity of direction was needed, the former president of the state-owned Philippine Deposit Insurance Corp and former Citibank executive said in a statement.
"The PSE appeals to all the key players of the Philippine capital market: let us all work together and join our hands. We are all in this together," he said.

"Let us form a united front and sharpen our competitive edge in carving our share in the global economy, not wasting our resources against one another," he added. "Let us focus on getting a bigger slice of investments, foreign and domestic alike. Only then will we reach our goal of being world class."
The PSE is currently regulated by the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), and they have clashed several times in what some market analysts have likened to a "turf war."
Nanagas told Reuters last week that a mechhanism would be in place so that companies issuing shares would not have to grapple with the different requirements of the PSE and the SEC.
Currently, a company has to seek permission from the SEC to sell shares and also go to the PSE to have those shares listed at the exchange.
PSE is seeking self-regulatory organisation status from the SEC, and Nanagas has said it hopes to get it by November 12.
This would involve installing an effective surveillance system to clamp down on insider trading and price manipulation.
Nanagas said the PSE was poised to become a major player in the global economy. "It is our goal to have a deeper, broader and bigger market," he said in his statement.
But he said there was a need to sustain ongoing reforms, including strengthening surveillance functions and the introduction of non-broker board members.
